To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ethylene, ethane, acetaldehyde and alcohol are produced by plants under stress, that the production of these compounds can be used to assess stress, and that these compounds can be measured simultaneously in the gas-phase by head space analysis.
plants exposed to a variety of stresses produce acetaldehyde and ethanal in addition to the previously known stress compounds ethylene, ethane, and ethanol.
plants exposed to air pollutants produce acetaldehyde and ethylene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an assay for the detection and measurement of plant stress.
the effects of air pollutants on plant physiology.
the development of a simple, rapid and sensitive method of monitoring air pollution stress on plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress induced by SO(2) exposure causes an increase of the production of acetaldehye and ethanol by plants.
ethylene, ethane, acetaldehyde and ethanal production is a good indicator of plant stress.
the four compounds are not a good method of measuring stress, but they are a useful tool for measuring stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of acetaldehydes, ethanol, ethane, and ethylene by plants under stress is a valuable tool for monitoring plant stress.
the production of acetaldehydes and ethanols in plants is not related to hypoxia.
plants exposed to air pollution, freezing, and water deficit produce ethylene, acetylene (ethylene + ethane), ethane, acetaldehyde and/or ethanol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acetaldehyde and ethane can be used to monitor stress in plants.
plants can produce acetaldehyde and ethanal as part of their response to stress and that these compounds are not just by-products of microbial metabolism.
the measurement of ethylene and ethanol in the gas phase is a simple and sensitive method for assessing plant stress.
